name: Sleep time
seoDesc: Sleep time: work out first sleep cycle's length from the time to fall asleep. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Sleep time calculator returns first sleep cycle's length from the 5 fields on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Sleep time calculator work?
sections.html:
The Sleep time calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports first sleep cycle's length in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the target waking up time); then you type in the time to fall asleep.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in minutes.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 96 options, such as 5:00 AM, 5:15 AM and 5:30 AM. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “Enter custom sleep cycle lengths”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Sleep time calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

First sleep cycle's length=-time to fall asleep − 5 × next sleep cycles' length − St6 + target waking up time
First sleep cycle's length=-time to fall asleep − 4 × next sleep cycles' length − St5 + target waking up time
St4=-time to fall asleep − first sleep cycle's length − 3 × next sleep cycles' length + target waking up time
First sleep cycle's length=-time to fall asleep − 2 × next sleep cycles' length − St3 + target waking up time
First sleep cycle's length=-time to fall asleep − next sleep cycles' length − St2 + target waking up time
St1=-time to fall asleep − first sleep cycle's length + target waking up time

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — Time to fall asleep = 15, Target waking up time set to 5:00 AM, First sleep cycle's length = 90 and Next sleep cycles' length = 90 — it reports st6 = -534, st5 = -444, st4 = -354 and st3 = -264.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: st6 = -534, st5 = -444, st4 = -354 and st3 = -264 should be roughly the size you expected from Time to fall asleep = 15 and Target waking up time set to 5:00 AM.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Sleep time calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the time to fall asleep — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Sleep time calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns first sleep cycle's length, derived from the time to fall asleep. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Sleep time calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the time to fall asleep, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports st6 = -534. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Sleep time calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
